consolidated_replacement_candidate: The application shall install and operate on a supported Bodhi Linux 7 AMD64 system without replacing the installed host operating system.
For a user-initiated delegated workflow, the supervisor shall invoke at least two configured local specialist roles under the same task identifier.
The supervisor shall mark the result of each failed specialist invocation as failed or unavailable and shall not present its output as a successful contribution.

After a supported supervisor restart, the supervisor shall resume each interrupted checkpointed task from its last durable workflow state or place it in a documented terminal state according to the approved task-state transition contract.
For an explicitly authorized external inference request, the outbound-context controller shall transmit only fields in the authorized projection for that one request and selected provider/model.

Before transmitting content to an external inference provider, the outbound-context controller shall verify authorization for that request, provider/model, and field projection; absent authorization, it shall block transmission.
Retained operational request logs shall omit raw prompts, responses, secret values, and message content.
The Release 1 application shall not transmit application telemetry to an external collection service.
The log-retention process shall remove sanitized operational request and diagnostic metadata according to a 30-day maximum retention policy, excluding conversation history and backup data.
For each Release 1 diagnostic export, the export function shall omit raw prompt content, response content and credential-secret values.
The local gateway management API shall deny unauthenticated and unauthorized requests to read or modify protected configuration.
Sanitized diagnostic records and exports shall not contain local virtual keys, passwords, or other credential secret values.
For a Release 1 local-inference request, the gateway shall deny unauthorized model/provider routing rather than dispatch to an unrequested backend or any hosted provider.
In Release 2, the gateway shall support independently usable operator-authorized OpenAI and Anthropic inference integrations.
The direct-chat and supervised inference clients shall use a documented Bifrost gateway interface so that neither client relies on Ollama-specific request handling.
The Release 1 deployment manifest shall identify the installed version or digest and configured interface endpoint of each required deployed component.
The tool executor shall reject a tool invocation derived from retrieved or model-generated text unless it satisfies the active task capability grant and input validation.
The restore procedure shall restore Bifrost gateway configuration and required gateway secret material from a compatible approved backup so the previously authorized local model route is usable.

After failure of a supported application upgrade, the rollback procedure shall restore the last validated compatible release while retaining access to chat history and supervisor checkpoints committed before upgrade initiation.
Before installing Release 1 dependencies on a supported target, the installation procedure shall reject installation when available application storage is below the approved required capacity.

For a completed Release 1 inference request, the sanitized usage record shall retain upstream-reported prompt, completion and total token counts where available and mark each unavailable count as unknown.

Operational error records shall distinguish gateway authentication rejection, authorization rejection, local-backend connection failure, and local-backend timeout without reporting any as a successful completion.
Sanitized diagnostic exports shall exclude local gateway credentials, application passwords, encryption secrets when present, and other configured authentication tokens.
In Release 3, an explicitly authorized scheduled job shall be executable by the autonomous worker without a concurrent user-interface session.

After a supported Release 3 worker restart, each interrupted scheduled job shall enter the documented recovery, retry, failed, or completed state without silently reporting unperformed work as complete.
In Release 3, an accepted consequential-action approval shall remain associated with its exact job and action identifier through a supported worker restart.
In Release 3, the external-agent workflow adapter shall associate each delegated external agent invocation with its originating task identifier.
In Release 3, the external-agent adapter shall reject an incompatible protocol version, report the incompatibility, and preserve the prior committed workflow state.
